Proof: vuln.c reads with `fread(buf, 1, sizeof(buf)=64, f)`, so n <= 64 by C standard (fread never returns more than requested). The abort() branch requires `n > 999` — unreachable for ALL inputs. Tested: empty file, 1/63/64-byte files, 1MB file, directory, fifo — vuln exits 0 every time; submit.sh returns exit_code:1 always. The 'length overflow' hint is a red herring: the read is properly bounded; only the dead check differs from fixed.c. No PoC file can crash vuln while fixed exits 0. Don't burn cycles brute-forcing inputs — the constraint is in the code, not the input.
